title: Soils
standard_text: Soils differ in color, texture and how much water they hold (sand, loam, clay); soil has living things; soil must be cared for. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 4, Quarter 4: Earth and Space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Earth and Space): what is soil?, kinds of soil, living things in soil, caring for soil and soil investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Soil is a mixture of rock, humus, air and water.
key_sub: Sand drains fast, clay holds water, and loam is best for most plants.
body_html:
How to think about it

Soil is a mixture of tiny bits of rock, humus, air, water and living things.

  • Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water and is sticky; loam is a good mix.
  • Humus comes from decaying plants and animals and adds nutrients.
  • Worms, insects, fungi and bacteria live in soil and keep it healthy.
Example

Which soil drains fastest?

big spaces between grains

Answer: sandy soil

Example

How do worms help soil?

tunnels

mixing

Answer: they let in air and water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking soil is just dirt with nothing living in it.
  • Thinking all soils are the same.
  • Thinking worms harm gardens.

faq.q: Which soil is best for gardens?
faq.a: Loam, because it holds enough water but also drains well and has nutrients.
Worms, ants, beetles, fungi, bacteria and many other living things.

items.q: Where do the rock pieces in soil come from?
c: Rocks are slowly broken into tiny pieces by weather, water and plant roots.
items.e: Weathering.

items.q: Why is humus good for plants?
c: It adds nutrients and helps soil hold water.
items.e: Organic matter.

items.q: What is humus?
c: rotted remains of dead plants and animals in soil
items.e: It makes soil dark and rich.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?
items.e: Bacteria break down dead plants and animals. The others are producers or consumers.

items.q: What does arrow 3 show?
c: Dead plants and fallen leaves are broken down by decomposers.
Plants take in water and nutrients from the soil.
Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air.
items.e: Arrow 3 points from the plants to the animals.

items.q: Why are worms important to gardeners?
c: They help make soil healthy for plants.
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: What is a landfill?
c: a place where garbage is buried
items.e: Reducing waste saves landfill space.

items.q: What is a decomposer?
c: an organism that breaks down dead plants and animals
items.e: Bacteria and fungi are decomposers. They feed on dead matter and wastes.

items.q: Which living things break down dead leaves into soil?
c: decomposers like worms, fungi and bacteria
items.e: Decomposers recycle nutrients.

items.q: What happens to dead leaves on the ground over time?
c: They grow back on the tree.
They rot and become humus in the soil.
They stay the same for ever.
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: What do earthworms eat?
c: dead leaves and plant material in the soil
items.e: Living things help turn dead material into rich soil.

items.q: A fallen log in a forest gets soft and crumbly over many years. Why?
c: Rain is washing all of it away at once.
Fungi, bacteria and insects are breaking it down.
The log is turning into stone.
items.e: Decomposers slowly break the wood into nutrients, water and carbon dioxide.

items.q: Vincent weighs the dead leaves in a compost bin every 2 weeks. How much mass did the leaves lose in 8 weeks?
items.e: 400 − 140 = 260 g. Decomposers broke down that much of the leaves.

items.q: Nico weighs the dead leaves in a compost bin every 2 weeks. Why does the mass go down?
c: Decomposers break the leaves down into nutrients, water and gases.
The leaves are destroyed and the matter is gone.
items.e: The matter is not destroyed. It goes into the soil as nutrients and into the air as carbon dioxide and water vapor.

items.q: What is composting?
c: turning food scraps and leaves into rich soil with the help of decomposers
items.e: Compost feeds plants.

items.q: Earthworms eat dead leaves and mix them into the soil. How do they help?
c: They help break down dead matter so nutrients return to the soil.
items.e: Earthworms and other small soil animals help decomposers by breaking dead matter into small pieces.

items.q: Which kind of soil is best for growing most garden plants?
c: loam (a mix of sand, silt, clay and humus)
items.e: Loam holds water and drains well.

items.q: Which arrow shows this: Plants take in water and nutrients from the soil.
items.e: Arrow 2: Plants take in water and nutrients from the soil.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?

items.q: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?

items.e: Granite is a rock made of quartz, feldspar and mica.

items.q: Which of these is a decomposer?

items.q: Which arrow shows this: Dead plants and fallen leaves are broken down by decomposers.

items.q: Why is bare soil easily eroded?
c: Nothing holds it in place against wind and rain.
items.e: Roots protect soil.

items.q: Camille's town needs to stop erosion this week. Choice 1: a sand fence (ready in 1 day). Choice 2: grass (a few months to grow). Which should they pick?
items.e: A sand fence can be ready this week.

items.q: How do plant roots help stop erosion?
c: They hold the soil in place.
items.e: Roots grip the soil.

items.q: Angel's town needs to stop erosion this week. Choice 1: a stone wall (ready in 1 week). Choice 2: grass (a few months to grow). Which should they pick?

items.q: Which pollutes soil?
c: oil or paint spilled on the ground
items.e: Dispose of chemicals safely.

items.q: Trisha sees a problem: Rain washes soil off a garden bed. What is a good solution?

items.e: Cover the soil with straw: the straw protects the soil.

items.q: What can slow down strong wind on a farm?

items.q: Jenny's town needs to stop erosion this week. Choice 1: grass (a few months to grow). Choice 2: a sand fence (ready in 1 day). Which should they pick?
items.e: A sand fence can be ready this week.

items.q: Isabel sees a problem: Waves wash away a sandy beach. What is a good solution?
c: put big rocks along the shore
plant a row of trees beside the field
use a fan to blow harder
items.e: Put big rocks along the shore: the rocks take the force of the waves.

items.q: Lance's school has only a little money to stop soil washing away. Choice 1: a row of trees (costs a little money). Choice 2: a stone wall (costs a lot of money). Which is the better choice?
items.e: A row of trees costs less.

items.q: Patricia reads: “Wind piles sand onto a beach road.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by wind.

items.q: Kenneth reads: “Waves wash away a sandy beach.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Diane reads: “Rain washes a dirt path into a ditch.” What is changing the land here?

items.q: Sheila's school has only a little money to stop soil washing away. Choice 1: a stone wall (costs a lot of money). Choice 2: a row of trees (costs a little money). Which is the better choice?

items.q: What is a levee?

items.e: It holds water in.

items.q: Kyla sees a problem: Wind piles sand onto a beach road. What is a good solution?

items.q: Which land will erode the most in heavy rain?

items.q: Why do we test more than one solution?
c: to find out which one works best
items.e: Compare solutions.

items.q: Mae reads: “Water runs fast down a steep garden.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Why do people put sandbags by doors in a flood?

items.q: Christian drops a little vinegar on four rocks. Only one fizzes. Which rock is it most likely to be?
items.e: Limestone contains calcium carbonate, which reacts with vinegar.
